name: Starter: Hindi
about: Hindi word order and endings in real, everyday sentences.

concept.line: In a plain Hindi sentence the verb comes at the end, after the object and the place: मैं चाय पीता हूँ (I tea drink).
होना (to be) changes for the person: मैं हूँ (I am), वह है (he, she, it is), हम, आप and वे हैं (we, you, they are), तुम हो (you are, to a friend); था, थी and थे are was and were.

words.means: मेरी = my; मेरे = my; मेरा = my

concept.line: का, के or की means of or 's, and matches the thing owned, not the owner: पापा की गाड़ी (Dad's car; गाड़ी is feminine).
तुम is you to a friend or family, with हो and -ओ; आप is polite, for strangers and elders, with हैं and -इए.
For habits and general states, use the verb's stem with -ता, -ती or -ते and होना: मैं चाय पीता हूँ (I drink tea); मेरी बहन दिल्ली में रहती है (my sister lives in Delhi).

words.means: रहता = live; रहते = live; रहती = lives
जाता = go; जा = going; जाती = goes
रहे = to live, to stay; auxiliary marking an ongoing action

concept.line: Every noun is masculine or feminine, and adjectives in -आ, and the verb forms that agree, change to match: अच्छा खाना, बड़ी रसोई; वह रहता है or रहती है; मैं करूँगा or करूँगी (a man or a woman).

words.means: जाना = to go; जाऊँगा = will go
